newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries flat in London, five-years busy.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries flat in London, five-years busy.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were flat to slightly bid in London on Tuesday, with the five-year sector attracting some swap activity, traders said.
"We're a little better bid in the five-year note," a trader at a U.S. bank in London said. "As has been the case for the past week, corporate issuance is running our market here."
A $500 million five-year issue from EDF, priced to yield 12 basis points over Treasuries sparked the early swap activity, he said.
The five-year note was quoted at 100-01, yielding 6.493 pct, compared with 99-31 at the close in Tokyo and New York on Monday.
The long bond was quoted at 96-17, flat on Tokyo and New York levels. The trader said the long end faced selling pressure.
"I'm hearing there are a lot of buy orders below the market but I've seen better selling," he said.
April leading indicators at 1400 GMT would provide a slight diversion for the market until key payroll data on Friday, economists said.
Dick Howard, senior economist at Bank Julius Baer in London, said the data could be supportive.
"The are really not showing much growth," he said.
Economists surveyed by Reuters showed a consensus forecast of unchanged from a 0.1 percent rise in March. --Jacqueline Thorpe, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 6176
